articles.title: Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management
articles.snippet:
Trebellar has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand its AI-native platform for corporate real estate management. Blossom Capital led the round, with participation from Haystack, Alt Capital, 1Flourish and Bynd.
The post Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Trebellar Raises $18 Million Series A To Bring AI To Corporate Real Estate Management
Trebellar has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand its AI-native platform for corporate real estate management. Blossom Capital led the round, with participation from Haystack, Alt Capital, 1Flourish and Bynd.
Trebellar is developing an AI-driven system of record intended to help enterprise real estate teams manage information that has traditionally been spread across spreadsheets, PDFs and separate software systems.
The platform combines information involving leases, space, employee headcount and utilization into a unified view.
Trebellar also incorporates commute times, transit access and employee sentiment to help corporate real estate teams evaluate whether properties are meeting organizational needs.
Rather than providing only a static analysis, the platform tracks the reasoning behind real estate decisions, their subsequent results and potential next actions.
Current customers include Meta, Uber, Merck and Cohesity.
The company was founded by engineers and operators with experience at Salesforce, Google, Waymo and Verkada alongside professionals with corporate real estate expertise.
Trebellar recently added Dave Radcliffe as an adviser. Radcliffe oversaw substantial growth of Google’s real estate portfolio during the tenures of Eric Schmidt, Larry Page and Sundar Pichai.
The company plans to use the Series A to expand its engineering and go-to-market teams, strengthen its AI capabilities and add enterprise customers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Real estate has been the one back-office function still running on spreadsheets and outside consultants. We built Trebellar to give leaders the independence to make these decisions themselves, with the same speed and confidence every other part of the business already has.”
Diego Ferreiro Val, Co-Founder and CEO of Trebellar
“What Trebellar has built is exactly what corporate real estate has been missing: Purpose-built AI that actually thinks about the problem the way we do, not just another dashboard. It’s quickly becoming a key part of how our team thinks about real estate decisions.”
Dave Gunter, VP of Global Workplace Services at Meta
“Corporate real estate is one of the last major categories AI hasn’t reached yet, not because the opportunity isn’t there, but because the problem needed technology built specifically for it, not a repurposed dashboard or another services relationship. Diego, David, and Adam are the right team to build that.”
Ophelia Brown, Blossom Capital

articles.title: W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform
articles.snippet:
W4 Games has raised $18 million in Series B funding to expand its international team, accelerate development of its enterprise technology and support growing commercial adoption of the open-source Godot Engine. The round was led by Tencent, with participation from OSS Capital, Lux Capital, Naval Ravikant and Tobias Lütke's family office.
The post W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
W4 Games Raises $18 Million Series B To Expand Godot Enterprise Platform
W4 Games has raised $18 million in Series B funding to expand its international team, accelerate development of its enterprise technology and support growing commercial adoption of the open-source Godot Engine. The round was led by Tencent, with participation from OSS Capital, Lux Capital, Naval Ravikant and Tobias Lütke’s family office.
The financing brings W4 Games’ total funding to $33 million.
W4 Games also signed a multi-year strategic partnership with Tencent focused on expanding the company’s business and the broader Godot ecosystem in Asia.
Under the partnership, W4 Games and Tencent will work together on go-to-market initiatives, localization, ecosystem development, advocacy and market development aimed at increasing Godot adoption among enterprises, game studios and developers throughout the region.
W4 Games was founded by core Godot developers and contributors to provide commercial technology, cloud services, professional support and other tools for studios building games with the open-source engine.
The company plans to use the Series B financing to increase its international workforce by approximately 50% and continue expanding its enterprise products.
Godot is an MIT-licensed open-source game engine stewarded by the independent nonprofit Godot Foundation.
W4 Games said Godot adoption has increased substantially over the past several years. According to SteamDB data cited by the company, the number of games built with Godot and published on Steam grew more than 50% year-over-year in both 2024 and 2025.
W4 Games’ analysis of Gamalytic data also found that the number of Godot-built games generating more than $1 million in annual sales increased from two to more than 50 during the past three years.
The company also pointed to growing adoption among younger developers. Godot’s share of submissions to events including Global Game Jam and GMTK Game Jam increased from approximately 10% in 2022 to 50%.
W4 Games plans to continue contributing technology created through its enterprise work back to the Godot project when possible, allowing improvements developed for commercial customers to benefit the broader open-source community.
KEY QUOTES:
“This collaboration with Tencent marks an important next step for W4 Games as we expand globally and bring Godot to more studios and developers. With Tencent as both a strategic partner and an investor, we have an opportunity to accelerate the adoption of enterprise-ready Godot technologies, particularly in Asia, while continuing to strengthen the open-source ecosystem that sits at the heart of everything we do.”
Nicola Farronato, Co-CEO of W4 Games
“Over the past few years, Godot has emerged as one of the world’s fastest-growing game engine technologies, with W4 Games at the forefront of its adoption by major studios and enterprises. We’re excited to work with Tencent to build on the momentum and further establish Godot Engine as a leading platform for companies creating the next generation of video games.”
Juan Linietsky, Godot Engine Creator and Founder of W4 Games

articles.snippet:

Existing investor Lavrock Ventures participated alongside Booz Allen Ventures, Sands Capital and Langford Industries.

articles.text:
Aventra Raises $17.5 Million To Scale Piranha Autonomous Precision Payload System
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Aventra Raises $17.5 Million To Scale Piranha Autonomous Precision Payload System
Aventra Defense Systems has raised $17.5 million in strategic financing led by Konvoy to scale production of its Piranha autonomous precision payload platform and develop additional long-range strike, one-way attack and intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems. Existing investor Lavrock Ventures participated alongside Booz Allen Ventures, Sands Capital and Langford Industries.
The financing also includes a funding facility from Western Alliance Bank.
Aventra plans to move Piranha from field-evaluation quantities into low-rate initial production while expanding manufacturing capacity at its facility in Herndon, Virginia.
The company will also increase flight testing and demonstrations with additional military services, combatant commands and allied partners.
Aventra intends to qualify additional payload and communications configurations spanning ISR, electronic warfare and kinetic missions.
The funding will also support hiring across engineering and manufacturing and the development of an additional platform that has not yet been announced.
Piranha uses high-altitude balloons and stratospheric air currents to carry autonomous payload systems over long distances.
The company is positioning the system as a lower-cost alternative for delivering ISR and precision effects compared with conventional long-range platforms.
Founded in 2025, Aventra has already deployed Piranha in U.S. Army exercises, including Arcane Thunder 26, along with additional evaluations and testing involving U.S., allied and partner forces.
The company said Piranha has completed approximately 400 flights demonstrating autonomous stratospheric reentry, long-range glide and delivery of kinetic and ISR effects.
Aventra said it has also secured its first series of delivery contracts as the system moves toward production.
KEY QUOTES:
“In under a year and with a lean capital investment, we took Piranha from concept to field deployment overseas, secured our first series of delivery contracts, and matured the system into a fully integrated platform. Today’s conflicts and the wars of the future will be won with volume, persistence, and affordability, which is why we’re working so hard to deliver more range and more kinetic effect. By using high-altitude balloons and stratospheric air currents to carry mass downrange without burning fuel, our approach delivers effects at greater distances, from higher altitudes, and at a fraction of the cost of conventional standoff munitions. We are leveraging physics to reshape economics and put cost-effective tools in the hands of the warfighter.”
Michael Weigand, Co-Founder and CEO of Aventra Defense Systems
“Affordable mass is ultimately a manufacturing problem. The Pentagon needs low-cost autonomous systems in volumes the traditional industrial base was never built to deliver. Aventra pairs a design that is inherently inexpensive to produce with a team that has already put hardware in operators’ hands at breakneck speed. That combination of resilient supply, scalable production, and proven field performance is exactly what our critical industries thesis is built around.”
Jason Chapman, General Partner at Konvoy

articles.title: University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award
articles.snippet:
A University of Maryland-led project received a $17.3 million National Science Foundation award to create an AI-powered and remotely accessible laboratory for biomanufacturing research. The four-year initiative, called the Collaborative for the Realization of Autonomous Biomanufacturing Lab, or CRAB Lab, will combine artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and real-time biological measurements.
The post University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
University Of Maryland-Led Biomanufacturing Lab Receives $17.3 Million NSF Award
A University of Maryland-led project received a $17.3 million National Science Foundation award to create an AI-powered and remotely accessible laboratory for biomanufacturing research. The four-year initiative, called the Collaborative for the Realization of Autonomous Biomanufacturing Lab, or CRAB Lab, will combine artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and real-time biological measurements.
The laboratory will be housed at the Institute for Bioscience and Biotechnology Research in Rockville, Maryland, while allowing researchers elsewhere in the U.S. to remotely access its capabilities.
The project is led by William Bentley, Robert E. Fischell Distinguished Professor and Director of the Robert E. Fischell Institute for Biomedical Devices.
University of Maryland Department of Computer Science Assistant Professor Alan Zaoxing Liu is a co-principal investigator alongside Gregory Payne, Martha Wang, and Hussain Dahodwala.
Ang Li of UMD’s Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering is co-leading the project’s AI efforts.
The CRAB Lab is one of 20 Programmable Cloud Laboratory Node sites supported by an NSF initiative focused on developing AI-enabled infrastructure for automated science and engineering.
Researchers will be able to program workflows that design, conduct, and analyze biomanufacturing experiments remotely.
Automated laboratory instruments and AI systems will collect information during experiments and help determine what actions should be taken next.
Liu’s research group is responsible for developing the data and AI infrastructure supporting the laboratory.
This work includes managing large volumes of measurement data, coordinating experiments from beginning to end, and developing models capable of identifying what Liu describes as biological vital signs.
Those signals could help determine whether a biomanufacturing process is operating as intended or beginning to deviate from expected conditions.
The project will also use bioelectronic measurement technologies developed through University of Maryland partnerships with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The technologies are designed to generate high-volume and high-speed biological measurements that can be used to train AI models.
Those models could identify combinations of measurements linked to product quality and other characteristics while experiments are still underway.
The CRAB Lab is expected to initially serve 30 biopharmaceutical companies through the Advanced Mammalian Biomanufacturing Innovation Center.
Remote access is also intended to make sophisticated automated laboratory infrastructure available to researchers at institutions that may not have comparable equipment of their own.
The initiative could ultimately help researchers accelerate experimentation related to medicines including vaccines and cancer therapies while improving reproducibility and reducing the time required to move from an idea to experimental results.

articles.title: Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
articles.snippet:
Hephaestus has emerged from stealth after raising $17.2 million to advance rare-earth-free high-temperature superconducting materials and develop a fusion reactor based on negative triangularity plasma geometry. The latest funding round was led by CiRi Ventures, with existing investors including Prescience Ventures, Teampact Ventures, Climate Capital, Unruly Capital, and CiRi Ventures.
The post Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Hephaestus Raises $17.2 Million To Advance Rare-Earth-Free Superconductors And Fusion Power
Hephaestus has emerged from stealth after raising $17.2 million to advance rare-earth-free high-temperature superconducting materials and develop a fusion reactor based on negative triangularity plasma geometry. The latest funding round was led by CiRi Ventures, with existing investors including Prescience Ventures, Teampact Ventures, Climate Capital, Unruly Capital, and CiRi Ventures.
Founded in London in 2019, Hephaestus is focused on reducing two significant cost and scalability challenges associated with fusion power: the high-temperature superconducting magnets used to confine plasma and edge-localized modes, or ELMs, that can increase the complexity and cost of conventional tokamak designs.
The company used an AI-based plasma solver to evaluate a broad range of tokamak design parameters and identified negative triangularity as a potentially lower-cost configuration. Negative triangularity reverses the conventional D-shaped plasma geometry used in many tokamaks.
Hephaestus said subsequent results from research facilities including DIII-D, JET, and SMART have demonstrated that negative triangularity can provide strong plasma performance without ELM instabilities.
The company moved into hardware development with Anvil 0, which it completed in 2024. Hephaestus describes the device as the world’s first tokamak designed specifically for negative triangularity from its inception.
Hephaestus is also developing high-temperature superconducting materials using its proprietary MaDi-AI materials discovery platform. The company said it has identified, manufactured, and characterized multiple novel HTS materials at laboratory scale, with validation from the U.K.’s National Physical Laboratory.
Most HTS magnets currently used in fusion rely on REBCO, or rare-earth barium copper oxide. Hephaestus is developing alternatives that do not use rare-earth materials, with the goal of making superconductors less expensive to manufacture, easier to scale, and less dependent on geographically concentrated supply chains.
The new funding will support the company’s next major milestones. Hephaestus plans to begin HTS manufacturing at a new 70,000-square-foot facility in New Jersey in 2027.
By 2030, the company is targeting a demonstration of the commercial potential of negative triangularity through a net-energy-gain reactor designed to achieve Q greater than 1.
Hephaestus has also begun early-access discussions with other fusion developers interested in sourcing its HTS technology. The company is expanding hiring across its New Jersey, London, and Rome locations as it builds both its materials manufacturing capabilities and fusion development program.
KEY QUOTES:
“Fusion has the potential of adding tens of GW’s per year of clean stable power to the grid, but that only happens if it becomes affordable and scalable. That’s why we chose negative triangularity, and why we’re manufacturing our own novel HTS magnets, to realise fusion’s full industrial potential.”
Jack Zamattio, CEO And Founder Of Hephaestus

articles.title: Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation
articles.snippet:
Hunt Capital Partners, Riverstone Platform Partners and Kansas City Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry have closed financing for a $17.1 million rehabilitation of The Alexandria, a 55-unit affordable housing community in Kansas City, Missouri.
The post Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Hunt Capital Partners Closes Financing For $17.1 Million Kansas City Affordable Housing Rehabilitation
Hunt Capital Partners, Riverstone Platform Partners and Kansas City Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry have closed financing for a $17.1 million rehabilitation of The Alexandria, a 55-unit affordable housing community in Kansas City, Missouri.
The property is located at 1328 E. Armour Boulevard and consists of two four-story buildings originally constructed separately in 1923.
The buildings were later connected through a shared elevator and lobby system and were most recently renovated using Low-Income Housing Tax Credit equity in 2006.
The Alexandria was 94% occupied at the time of the financing and had a waiting list of six qualified households.
The project will preserve 55 studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom homes serving households earning up to 30% and 60% of area median income.
All 55 homes will be covered by a 20-year Project-Based Section 8 Housing Assistance Payment contract.
The property has historically operated under a Section 8 HAP agreement that expires in 2029 and is expected to be renewed for another 20 years.
Planned improvements include upgrades to security, a secured and gated parking lot, building access and video surveillance.
Residents will also have access to voluntary supportive services including budget counseling, employment coaching, housing stabilization assistance and health and wellness programs.
The capital stack includes $9.1 million of federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Hunt Capital Partners and $6.4 million of state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Monarch Private Capital.
UMB Bank provided a $13 million construction loan, while Cedar Rapids Bank & Trust provided a $4.5 million permanent loan.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are honored to once again work alongside Riverstone Platform Partners, Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry, and UMB Bank to provide affordable housing in the Kansas City metro area. The rehabilitation of The Alexandria will preserve homes for families who need them the most.”
Jeff Weiss, President of Hunt Capital Partners
“Every week we see another affordable property somewhere in this country convert to market rate, drop out of its HAP contract or get run into the ground by an owner who has stopped reinvesting. The Alexandria is proof that there’s another way. The team stepped in, rebuilt the capital stack, and recommitted this property to affordability for decades. Fifty-five families get to stay in their homes, in their neighborhood, without the fear of displacement, and that’s the whole point of this work.”
Kelley Hrabe, Founder and Managing Partner of Riverstone Platform Partners
“We are proud to be the nonprofit partner of The Alexandria development that is not only preserving 55 homes of affordable housing but transforming them into beautiful places to live. We are excited to add this to our ever-growing portfolio of affordable housing.”
Scott Cooper, Executive Director of Kansas City Metropolitan Lutheran Ministry
“UMB is excited to play a role in the redevelopment of The Alexandria.
